![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226618/assets/9b3065e58decfca5355252b93ec3283cc5ffc96dc04826aeab1131e95d3a2e64.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the closed path along the rectangle, traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, ${y}_{1}={y}_{2},$ and we have

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y=0.
$$
